text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The government nominated Mohamad Shatah a new ambassador in Washington after the current ambassador ended his mandate.
-International credit agencies gave Lebanon its first credit ratings.
-Prime Minister Hariri said the expected visit of Pope John Paul II to Beirut on May 10 was a big sign of confidence in Lebanon.
-Merrill Lynch will expand its financial activities in Lebanon, deputy chairman of the financial group Zakkour said.
-Armenia's Foreign Minister will arrive in Lebanon on March 13 on a two-day official visit.
-Israeli shelling on inhabited areas in south Lebanon.
-The leftist opposition MP Wakim asks the government about the fate of Lebanese physician Oumayah Abboud who was arrested 12 days ago for suspected involvement with Japanese Red Army.
